title: Create Account
summary: Create Account describes adversary creation of new accounts to maintain access after an initial foothold is lost or remediated. The accounts involved can be local or domain user accounts, accounts holding administrative rights, cloud and SaaS identities, service principals, or machine accounts created through directory APIs, and they can be created on a single host, in the enterprise directory, or in a hosted tenant the organisation only partially monitors. The technique is favoured because a fresh account survives the password resets that remediation applies to compromised existing accounts, blends into the constant background churn of real onboarding, and can be granted additional rights quietly if the adversary already holds privilege. The mechanism usually involves ordinary administrative interfaces rather than exploits: command-line account management utilities, remote management protocols, directory and cloud identity APIs, and application-specific user administration consoles. The artefacts are concentrated in directory and audit telemetry, including account creation events, group membership additions, privilege role assignments, cloud provider audit records, and the authentication activity of the new identity afterwards. Benign account creation is continuous in most environments, driven by hiring, contractor onboarding, automation and service deployment, so an investigation should weigh the identity of the creator, the interval between creation and first use, the privileges requested or assigned, how naming and description conventions compare with organisational standards, and whether the creating identity was itself recently established or recently elevated. Accounts created and then used immediately, added straight into a privileged group, or authenticating from unexpected infrastructure are the cases that warrant escalation, and reviewing them against a documented joiner process is usually what separates a real incident from a noisy one.
objectives: Identify the account types an adversary can create and the visibility each provides to the defender.
Interpret directory, local and cloud audit records to reconstruct who created an account and when.
Detect create-and-use patterns by comparing account creation with subsequent authentication activity.
Evaluate naming, privilege and approval controls that make rogue accounts distinguishable from legitimate ones.
Explain how identity governance and periodic access review limit the lifetime of adversary accounts.
Write detection logic for privileged account creation and for sensitive group membership changes.
